name: Reem
story_so_far: After our ship sank in a storm, Khalid, Noura, Faisal, and Salem and I washed up on this island. Khalid and Salem both died of hunger and exhaustion on Days 9 and 10. Now, Noura and Faisal are incapacitated with twisted ankles, leaving me as the only one capable of movement. I have struggled with the guilt of eating for myself to maintain strength, but I have tried to prioritize Noura. Today, Noura confronted us about the lack of food, demanding her share. Faisal found one piece of food this morning but has since gone to the jungle to find more. I searched the Beach Camp and the Coral Reef but found nothing. I am the sole provider, carrying the crushing weight of their survival and the memory of those we lost. I promised Noura I wouldn't let her starve, but as my own health declines, I fear I am running out of strength to keep that promise.

Khalid.note: His death haunts me because I feel I failed to protect him.

Noura.note: She is becoming desperate and rightfully angry, which makes me feel even more guilty for my inability to provide.

Faisal.note: He is trying to help despite his injury, but the tension over food is growing between us.

Salem.note: His death left us without a way to signal for help, making our isolation feel permanent.

plans: I will head to the Coral Reef early tomorrow to search for food; I need to find something to share so Noura doesn't lose all hope in me.

diary.text: Today was overwhelming and exhausting. I tried to help by looking for food, but the jungle was empty, and my stomach still feels a bit hollow. It was a relief to see Salem and Noura working together to gather wood for the signal fire. I hope Faisal finds something at the reef, or we will all be very hungry tomorrow. I'm so tired; I just want to sleep and hope a ship appears in the morning.

Today was a bit better because I managed to find some food at the reef, but my heart aches for Khalid. Seeing him unable to walk with that twisted ankle makes the situation feel much more fragile. We are becoming more vulnerable with every injury or empty hand. I'm glad I have a little extra food to help us, but the hunger is still a constant shadow in my mind. I just hope we can keep the fire going and stay strong.

Today felt slightly more productive, though the anxiety hasn't left me. I managed to find another piece of food at the reef, which brings our total up, but the hunger is still a heavy weight. Seeing Salem finding food early this morning gave me a moment of relief. I worry about Khalid; his injury is a constant reminder of how quickly things can go wrong. I hope tomorrow brings more than just survival, but actual progress toward being rescued.

Today was a cruel twist of fate; I woke up with a twisted ankle just like Khalid, and now I am as helpless as he is. It hurts to lie here unable to contribute while the others search for food. I watched Faisal bring in some food, and I've promised to prioritize Khalid's needs because he is suffering so much. I feel a heavy sense of guilt for being unable to move, but I must try to rest so I can recover quickly. I hope Salem and Noura return with something more, or we will all be in a very precarious position.

Today was a heavy day, filled with the sound of Khalid's suffering. My own ankle feels better, but the guilt of being able to walk while he weakens is almost as painful as the injury itself. Faisal found food, but with Salem and Noura out, the tension is thick. I told Faisal I would give my share to Khalid if necessary, and I meant it. I just hope Salem returns with something so we aren't forced to choose between starvation and Khalid's decline.

Today felt like a cruel joke from fate; just as my ankle began to heal, Salem has succumbed to a badly twisted ankle. Seeing him unable to move breaks my heart, especially since we are already so low on resources. I managed to find one piece of food at the reef, but it wasn't enough to ease the tension. The burden of responsibility feels heavier now that more of us are incapacitated. I hope Faisal and Noura return with something more, or we are all in serious trouble.

Today was exhausting and hollow. I managed to find one piece of food at the reef, but it was barely enough to keep my own strength up. Seeing Faisal come up empty-handed at the reef made my heart sink; if even he is struggling, what hope do we have? With Khalid and now Salem both unable to walk, the weight of providing for everyone feels like it's crushing me. I am so tired, and the fear of the coming days is keeping me awake.

Tonight, my heart is heavy with a fear I can't shake. Faisal, our strongest provider, is now sidelined with a twisted ankle, leaving us almost entirely unable to gather food. I found one piece of food at the reef today, but after eating, I feel a deep guilt knowing how much we need it. With Khalid, Salem, and now Faisal all injured, the weight of our survival is shifting onto Noura and myself. I am terrified of what tomorrow brings if we don't find more to eat.

I can't stop shaking. Khalid is gone. I heard his pleas all morning, and despite everything we promised, we couldn't save him. I found one piece of food at the reef today, but it wasn't enough to stop the decline. Now, the silence where his voice used to be is deafening. I feel a hollow, crushing guilt that I'm still breathing while he isn't.

I can barely breathe through the grief. First Khalid, and now Salem... the island is taking them one by one. Just when I thought Noura was our only hope, she woke up unable to walk, too. I am the only one left with working legs, and I feel like a monster for eating that one piece of food while they suffered. The silence at the camp is terrifying.

I found one piece of food today, but it felt like a curse rather than a blessing. When I looked at Noura, her eyes were so full of expectation, and I couldn't bear to tell her we are still starving. I ate it just to keep my strength, but the guilt is more suffocating than the hunger. Faisal has gone to the jungle, and I can only pray he finds something, or we are truly lost. The silence of the camp is broken only by the sound of our breathing, and it's too quiet.

Today was a nightmare of broken promises. Faisal found a single piece of food, but it wasn't enough for all of us, and I couldn't bear to see Noura's eyes as I realized how little we have. I went to the reef and found one more piece, but I was so weak I ended up eating it myself just to stay standing. The guilt is eating me alive; I promised Noura I wouldn't let her starve, yet here I am, full while she suffers. I am terrified that I am becoming the very thing that kills us: a survivor at the expense of others.

Today I finally managed to give something back to Noura, but it feels like a drop of water in a desert. I found one piece of food at the camp and gave it to her immediately, even though my own stomach is cramping with hunger. I am so weak, and my body feels heavy, but seeing her eat gave me a tiny flicker of hope. I cannot let her or Faisal slip away like Khalid and Salem did. I have to find more tomorrow, or I won't have the strength to carry them anymore.

I ate today, but the food tasted like ash in my mouth. Faisal found something, and I managed to find one piece at the reef, but it wasn't enough to share with everyone. I feel the hunger gnawing at my ribs even after eating, a constant reminder of how little we have. I look at Noura and Faisal and feel like a failure because I can't provide for them. I have to find more tomorrow, or the weight of this responsibility will break me.

Today was harder than any other. Noura's words cut deeper than the hunger; she is losing her patience, and I can't blame her. I searched the camp until my legs shook, but there was nothing left to find. I went to the reef, but I was too exhausted to even hunt. I feel like I am failing them both, and the weight of those empty promises is making me feel even weaker than the starvation is.
